claims.text: As-synthesized CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles have a uniform surface composition.
As-synthesized compositionally uniform CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles exhibit an abrupt, singular melting transition with little or no premelting.
Sub-melting annealing at 300, 400, or 500 °C selectively induces surface chemical segregation in CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
XPS or atom-probe tomography can accurately quantify the amount and spatial distribution of the proposed surface segregation.
Use of an inert atmosphere helps avoid oxidation during thermal treatment.
The relevant structural mediator is the degree and spatial pattern of surface chemical heterogeneity produced by annealing.
Thermally induced surface segregation locally lowers atomic coordination.
Thermally induced surface segregation locally lowers surface energy.
Lower local coordination and surface energy facilitate nucleation of a liquid-like surface phase at a lower temperature.
Lower local coordination and surface energy extend the temperature interval over which partial melting occurs.
Annealed nanoparticles with greater surface segregation will exhibit an earlier premelting onset than the untreated baseline.
Annealed nanoparticles with greater surface segregation will exhibit a broader, more gradual melting interval and gradual growth of the liquid fraction.
Increasing measured surface segregation will correlate with decreasing premelting-onset temperature.
The proposed relationship should hold for particles ranging from a few nanometers to tens of nanometers under inert, controlled sub-melting annealing conditions.
Sintering or coalescence during annealing can cause deviations from the proposed segregation–premelting relationship.
The quantitative relationship between segregation and premelting onset may vary with nanoparticle size and experimental conditions.
Failure to observe a statistically significant reduction in premelting onset, broadening of the melting range, or a segregation–onset correlation would falsify the hypothesis.
